title: IBM webMethods

concepts.title: Setting Up a Productive Development Environment
Capstone: Build an Order-to-Cash Integration Platform

notes:
Requester's Notes field, verbatim: "The generic topics should be kept very light, The focus should be more webmethods specific topics." — so Part I and the vendor-neutral architecture chapters stay short and move quickly to how webMethods actually does it.

Parse reinterpretation (recorded per the conservative-parse rule): the issue's "Seed concepts" field was not a line-per-concept list but a full prose book proposal. Only its explicit numbered chapter headings (### 1 … ### 23) were taken as concepts[] entries, in the order given; the surrounding material was folded here and into research.json rather than dropped.

Requester's proposed full title (kept as the cover subtitle, since the issue's dedicated Title field said "IBM Webmethods"): "IBM webMethods in Practice: Enterprise Integration, APIs, Events, and Operations". Title casing normalized to the product's own orthography, webMethods.

Part structure from the request: I Foundations (1-4), II Building Integrations (5-11), III Reliability and Operations (12-16), IV Architecture and Modernization (17-21), V Capstone (22-23).

Audience: developers and integration architects. One realistic end-to-end business scenario runs through the whole book — order processing across a public API, an ERP, a SaaS CRM, and an event stream.

Requested positioning: emphasize design reasoning (why a pattern fits), production concerns (security, retries, monitoring, deployment, supportability), a continuous case study extending chapter to chapter, version resilience (concepts first, screen-by-screen product steps isolated), and modernization (webMethods alongside APIs, event streams, SaaS, containers and CI/CD rather than as a legacy ESB). Each implementation chapter should carry a short concept section, a guided build, a failure scenario, and design-review questions.

Requested appendices, folded into cheatsheet.html: terminology quick reference, integration design review checklist, API design checklist, production-readiness checklist, error taxonomy and retry matrix, sample canonical schemas and message contracts, glossary.
